\section[afirmar]{afirmar — to state, to say that something is so}

\label{lesson:ES-C480-afirmar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for in advance, then the Spanish for to replace.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: afirmar}
\textbf{afirmar} — \textquotedblleft{}to state, to say that something is so\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El director afirma que no hay problema.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The director states that there is no problem.}
\end{quote}

More formal than \emph{decir}; news reports use it a lot.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afirmar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afirmar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{afirmar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for in advance, then the Spanish for to replace, then say \emph{afirmar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does afirmar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To state, to say that something is so\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[comunicar]{comunicar — to communicate, to inform}

\label{lesson:ES-C480-comunicar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to replace, then the Spanish for to state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: comunicar}
\textbf{comunicar} — \textquotedblleft{}to communicate, to inform\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le comunicamos que su pedido ha llegado.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We inform you that your order has arrived.}
\end{quote}

In Spain, \emph{está comunicando} on the phone means the line is busy; elsewhere people say \emph{está ocupado}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{comunicar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{comunicar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to replace, then the Spanish for to state, then say \emph{comunicar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does comunicar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To communicate, to inform\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[interrumpir]{interrumpir — to interrupt}

\label{lesson:ES-C480-interrumpir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to state, then the Spanish for to communicate.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: interrumpir}
\textbf{interrumpir} — \textquotedblleft{}to interrupt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Perdona que te interrumpa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sorry to interrupt you.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Sin interrumpir} — without interrupting.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[prometer]{prometer — to promise}

\label{lesson:ES-C480-prometer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to communicate, then the Spanish for to interrupt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: prometer}
\textbf{prometer} — \textquotedblleft{}to promise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te prometo que vuelvo pronto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I promise you I will be back soon.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La promesa} is the promise.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[quejarse]{quejarse — to complain}

\label{lesson:ES-C480-quejarse}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to interrupt, then the Spanish for to promise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: quejarse}
\textbf{quejarse} — \textquotedblleft{}to complain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Los vecinos se quejan del ruido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The neighbours complain about the noise.}
\end{quote}

It goes with \emph{de}: \emph{quejarse de algo}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
